title: The STAND-IN skip gap (batch 22, 2026-09-20): host and Client1 merge, Client1 disconnects, so the HOST becomes the stand-in that simulates Client1's gym. The host then walks into that gym and skips 3 game-hours alone. Before this build nobody simulated the shop during the skip - native RunHourly exempts the shop the local player stands in, and the round-60 postfix that covers that exemption stood down because MergerFlip.TrulyMine is false on a merger-flipped stand-in shop. The gate is now MergerFlip.BooksHere, so the machine that holds the books is the machine that sims. Asserts: the host really is the stand-in for that gym, the occupied-shop hourly sim names the gym during the skip, and the gym's completed visits and till queue both rise across the skip. Ends dissolved; NO save.
preconditions: Fixture save1 (host melaus, client Client1). Dev build with merge / mergestatus / absence / regstate / enterbuilding / exitbuilding / skipvote / skipstate / salestats / clock / pause (BAMP_DEV) on both machines. THE SHOP is Client1's gym at vars.gym - step 14 checks at runtime, on the host, that the address is rented, is a gym (a customer-SPAWNING type, which the occupied-shop sim requires) and is merger-FLIPPED there, which is exactly the state that made TrulyMine answer false on the only machine running it. The client is DROPPED mid-run and relaunched at the end so the merger can be dissolved. NOTHING is ever saved.

steps.note: the worlds settle and the first interior/paperwork bundles cross

THE GAP'S PRECONDITION, on the machine that will stand in: the merger flip makes the partner's gym read rented=True here while the sync layer knows it is not ours, so MergerFlip.TrulyMine answers False - the old gate - although this is the only machine that will run the shop. It is also a customer-SPAWNING type, which the occupied-shop sim requires (data.spawnCustomers).
and on the OWNER the same address is genuinely theirs, before they drop
nobody is absent yet
sets the host's log search baseline before the disconnect
the owner drops out; the host designates itself and starts simulating the absent member's businesses

THE STAND-IN PREMISE, asserted: this machine is the designated stand-in for the absent owner AND this gym is in the set it simulates here. Without this the rest of the run would be vacuous - a shop nobody stands in for is simulated by nobody, correctly.
time must RUN - absolute semantics, a no-op when already running

OPENING HOURS: the fixture loads day 133 12:00, so 13:00 is forward and the 13:00->16:00 skip stays inside ordinary hours (IsBusinessOpen gates the occupied-shop sim). The lever only moves the clock FORWARD; an ERR means live time already passed 13:00 and the run continues.

THE STAND-IN STANDS IN THE SHOP HE BOOKS. Native BusinessSimulatorHelper.RunHourly (:32) exempts the customer-spawning shop the LOCAL player occupies, so from here on only our postfix can pay this gym during a skip.
the interior settles and the hour's shoppers start arriving
BASELINE immediately before the vote, on the stand-in. Captures only, so the whole skip is counted against this line.

THE HOST VOTES ALONE - the only connected player, so his own vote makes consensus and the skip starts on this step. THE ASSERTION OF THIS SCENARIO is the second line: the occupied-shop hourly sim names THIS gym during the skip. Before batch 22 that line could never appear here, because the postfix's TrulyMine gate stood down on a merger-flipped stand-in shop and native had already exempted it - the shop earned nothing for the whole skip.
report-only sample during the skip
report-only poll: has it finished?
the skip has stopped, at or after the goal it was racing to

THE MONEY ASSERTION: across the skip the absent owner's gym gained completed visits AND gained entries in its till queue (unprocessedCompletedOrders - `salestats` has no field literally called 'orders'; this count IS the orders waiting for the day roll). Both rising is the shop being simulated and booked on the stand-in's machine, which is what the whole scenario is about.
fixture hygiene: the stand-in leaves the gym
the absent owner returns so the merger can be dissolved
the host drops the stand-in simulator the moment the owner is back
FIXTURE HYGIENE: every merger scenario ENDS DISSOLVED; NO save
